name.value: Doctor Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden

description.value: The first full-scale traditional Ming Dynasty classical Chinese garden built outside of China, opened in 1986 in the heart of Vancouver's Chinatown. Named World's Top City Garden by National Geographic in 2011 and Canadian Garden of the Year in 2012, it was born from the community effort that defeated a proposed freeway through Chinatown and redirected Vancouver toward walking, cycling, and transit-oriented planning. Touring cyclists will find a tranquil cultural oasis steps from major urban cycling routes, offering guided garden and Chinatown walking tours, tea ceremonies, exhibitions, and a gift shop.

Contact details (phone, address, website) all corroborate between OSM and the website. No evidence on the website or in OSM tags for bike parking, water refill, washrooms, or any of the optional cycling-specific amenities. OSM wheelchair=yes is noted but not used as authoritative for specific amenity claims without website confirmation.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A nationally recognized heritage attraction and registered museum in central Vancouver, easily accessible by bike. A clear fit for a cycling tourism directory as a cultural destination, though cyclist-specific amenities could not be confirmed.

wow_evidence: First full-scale Ming Dynasty classical garden built outside China (1986); National Geographic World's Top City Garden 2011 — international recognition, verifiable first. Serene day-shaping visit.
